text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementHistoryThis Viking Dress Survived for 1,300 Years, Protected by Its Metal OrnamentsSuch delicate textiles typically decompose within a few yearsDNBy David Nield11:00 AM CDT on August 31, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleEvery so often, archaeologists come across something that’s beaten overwhelming odds to remain preserved across generations—such as a section of a 1,300-year-old Viking dress that was recently discovered in the western Jutland region of Denmark.Subscribe to skip adsFeatured VideoPowered By 10 Inside China's first spacewalks: astronauts recount a mock rescue missionShareNextStayOrdinarily, you’d expect such fabrics to decompose within a few years, which is why researchers describe the find as “absolutely magical” in a (translated) Facebook post. The artifact was excavated from the tomb of a young girl by the Archaeology West Jutland (ArkVest) project.A sketch showing how the girl may have looked.
